hypotheses.label: Predominantly organic mobilisation
hypotheses.description: Movement develops mainly through social conditions and decentralised participant action.
hypotheses.mechanism: Decentralised mobilisation without deliberate state enablement.
hypotheses.outcome: A large movement occurs without purposeful state facilitation.
predictions: Early messages have multiple independent origins.
Operational records show ordinary enforcement attempts.
disconfirmers: Authenticated orders instruct forces to reduce enforcement.
A single coordinated logistics chain predates public mobilisation.

hypotheses.label: Deliberate domestic-state exploitation
hypotheses.description: State actors knowingly permit or exploit an existing movement.
hypotheses.mechanism: Selective enforcement or deliberate operational permission.
hypotheses.timeframe: Before or during the defined event window.
hypotheses.outcome: An existing movement is used to create political pressure.
predictions: Enforcement changes depart from operational baseline.
Control can be restored quickly after political conditions change.
disconfirmers: Records show units were overwhelmed despite consistent orders.
Independent mobilisation predates any state response and enforcement remains consistent.

hypotheses.label: Organic movement later exploited

hypotheses.mechanism: Sequential organic mobilisation followed by deliberate state exploitation.
hypotheses.timeframe: Organic origin followed by later state action.
hypotheses.outcome: Both independent pressure and purposeful exploitation contribute.
predictions: State behaviour changes after the movement is already visible.
disconfirmers: Evidence shows complete pre-planning before organic mobilisation.
No material change in state behaviour occurs.

hypotheses.label: Foreign encouragement
hypotheses.description: Another state encourages relevant domestic action without direct command.
hypotheses.mechanism: Diplomatic signalling, intelligence contact or political inducement.
hypotheses.timeframe: Before or during the defined event window.

disconfirmers: No relevant contact exists despite records that should contain it.

hypotheses.label: Insufficient information

hypotheses.mechanism: Critical evidence remains absent, inaccessible or dependent.
hypotheses.outcome: No responsible attribution can be made.
predictions: Sensitivity to disputed evidence remains high.
disconfirmers: Independent authenticated records resolve the key causal questions.
